question: Which country is ranked 1st in the Global Firepower Index 2025 with the lowest Power Index score of 0.0744?
solution:
The correct answer is __**USA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **United States of America (USA)** has been ranked **1st** in the **Global Firepower (GFP) Index 2025**, maintaining its position as the world's most powerful military.
 
• The **USA** achieved the lowest and most favorable **Power Index (PwrIndx)** score of **0.0744**. In this indexing system, a score of **0.0000** is considered the "perfect" score, meaning the lower the numerical value, the higher the nation's theoretical fighting capability.
 
• The **2025 Global Firepower ranking** utilized more than **60 individual factors** to determine a given nation's **Power Index** score, ranging from military might and financials to logistical capability and geography.
 
• The assessment included a total of **145 world powers**, providing a comprehensive look at the conventional war-making capabilities of nations across the globe.
 
• The **USA** remains at the top due to its massive **defense budget**, advanced **technological integration**, and significant lead in **airpower** and **naval carrier** fleets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Top Ranked Nations in 2025**:

 
 
• **Russia**: Ranked **2nd** globally with a **Power Index** score of **0.0768**.
 
• **China**: Ranked **3rd** globally with a **Power Index** score of **0.0772**, closely trailing Russia.
 
• **India**: Ranked **4th** globally with a **Power Index** score of **0.1087**, solidifying its status as a major regional and global military power.
 
• **South Korea**: Ranked **5th**, showing significant growth in military manufacturing and exports.
 
 
 
• **Methodology of the Index**:
 
 
• The **Global Firepower Index** has been compiled since **2006**. It focuses strictly on **conventional capabilities** and does not take **nuclear stockpiles** into account for the direct score, though it considers them as a general strategic deterrent.
 
• Factors weighed include **manpower** (available population and active personnel), **equipment** (tanks, aircraft, naval units), **natural resources** (oil production/reserves), and **financial stability**.
 
• The ranking allows smaller, but more technologically advanced, nations to compete with larger, less-developed ones by applying specific **modifiers** (penalties and bonuses) to the raw data.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographic and Economic Factors**: The index rewards nations with high **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** and strong **logistical infrastructure**, such as **ports**, **terminals**, and **roadway networks**, as these are vital for sustaining long-term military operations.
 
• **Budgetary Dominance**: The **USA** defense budget remains the largest in the world, often exceeding **$800 billion**, which is greater than the next several countries combined. This enables the **United States** to maintain **11 nuclear-powered aircraft carriers**, a feat unmatched by any other nation.
 
• **Regional Trends**: In the **2025** report, there is a notable trend of **Asian nations** (specifically **China, India, and South Korea**) increasing their dominance in the top 5, reflecting a shift in global military investment toward the **Indo-Pacific** region.
